mythology: The Ashtadasha tradition honours Saraswati in Kashmir. In the Shankara Digvijaya tradition, Adi Shankaracharya ascends the Sarvajna Peetha after debate.
pilgrimage_significance: The ruins preserve the memory of Sharada worship and a historic centre of learning. The modern Teetwal shrine is a separate site.
historical_notes: The Neelum Valley ruins are represented with the 35 × 26 m field-survey enclosure, 63-step western approach, damaged double porch, southern break, eastern postern and raised roofless sanctuary. The square sanctuary has a 3.8 m interior and opens west. The north wall retains a recessed chamber described in the archaeological record.
